rēcta: the feminine of the adjective rēctus (tībia rēcta), not Lewis & Short’s adverb rectā
fidē: the ablative of fidēs (Lewis & Short fĭdes), not the adverb fīdē
peditum: the genitive plural of pedes, peditis (Lewis & Short pĕdes), not the participle of pēdō
ōvīs: the ablative plural of ōvum, egg (Lewis & Short ōvum), not ovis, sheep
ālīs: the ablative plural of āla, wing, not the archaic alis (alius)
jugīs: the ablative plural of jugum, ridge (Lewis & Short jŭgum), not the adjective jūgis
erō: the future of sum, not Lewis & Short’s ēro
tenēre: the infinitive of teneō, not the adverb tenerē
īmus: the first person plural of eō (īmus, ītis), not Lewis & Short’s headword ĭmus
Mātūrāte: the plural imperative of mātūrō, not the adverb mātūrātē
novī: the genitive of novus, not nōvī, the perfect of nōscō
modō: the ablative of modus (nūllō modō), not the adverb modo
Parce: the imperative of parcō, not the adverb parcē
Manē: the imperative of maneō, not māne, morning
